title: Building addition proofs inside Heyting arithmetic

based_on.title: Logic and Proof, §17.4 Defining Arithmetic Operations (HTML version 3.18.4)
based_on.pages: §17.4, recursion clauses, first four addition propositions/proofs; §18.2 only supplementary examples of the same induction patterns

summary: Construct internal HA addition proofs by induction with fixed parameters, then instantiate associativity, commutativity and cancellation at supplied terms.
abstract: The recursion equations for addition immediately give a proof that x plus zero equals x. Reversing the arguments requires an induction, and so do the familiar rearrangement and cancellation laws. We construct those arguments as finite proofs inside Heyting arithmetic, keeping every other variable fixed through each successor step. The resulting universal certificates apply to arbitrary arithmetic terms and to equations proved under additional assumptions. This makes the difference between calculating each standard numeral and building one uniform arithmetic proof concrete.
